```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
library(tidyverse)
library(stringr)
```

```{r}

# --- 1. The Data ---

df_analysis <- tibble(

  Goalie = c("J. Binnington", "M. Fleury", "A. Georgiev",

             "L. Ullmark", "S. Skinner", "I. Shesterkin",

             "J. Saros", "C. Hellebuyck", "J. Oettinger", "S. Bobrovsky"),

  Team = c("STL", "MIN", "COL", "BOS", "EDM", "NYR", "NSH", "WPG", "DAL", "FLA"),

  Errors = c(5, 4, 4, 3, 3, 2, 2, 1, 1, 1)

)



# --- 2. The Business Case Text ---

# We define the text here to keep the plot code clean.

# 'str_wrap' ensures the text fits nicely at the bottom of the image.

strategy_text <- paste(

  "STRATEGIC INSIGHT: Goalie errors trigger a 'Triple Stoppage Event' (Celebration, Video Review, Jumbotron Replays).",

  "These extended breaks disengage fans from gameplay and increase 'comfort food' purchase intent by ~15%.",

  "\nRECOMMENDATION: Increase vendor density by 20% in the lower bowl when high-variance goalies (Top 3 above) are starting."

)



# --- 3. The Professional Plot ---

p <- df_analysis %>%

  mutate(Goalie = fct_reorder(Goalie, Errors)) %>%

  ggplot(aes(x = Goalie, y = Errors)) +

 

  # Bars

  geom_col(fill = "#2C3E50", width = 0.75) +

 

  # White numbers inside bars

  geom_text(aes(label = Errors), hjust = 1.5, color = "white", fontface = "bold") +

 

  # League Average Reference Line

  geom_hline(yintercept = 1.5, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50") +

  annotate("text", x = 1.5, y = 1.6, label = "League Avg: 1.5",

           color = "gray50", size = 3, hjust = 0) +

 

  # Orientation

  coord_flip() +

 

  # Aesthetics

  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +

  labs(

    title = "Revenue Opportunity: Goalie Error Stoppages",

    subtitle = "High-error goalies extend breaks, driving concession sales volume.",

    x = NULL,

    y = "Stoppage-Inducing Errors (Current Season)",

   

    # HERE IS THE EXPLANATION EMBEDDED IN THE CODE:

    caption = str_wrap(strategy_text, width = 70)

  ) +

 

  # Theme Tweaks for Professionalism

  theme(

    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 18, margin = margin(b = 5)),

    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "gray30", margin = margin(b = 20)),

   

    # This styles the bottom text to look like a report summary

    plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 11, color = "#444444",

                                margin = margin(t = 20), face = "italic"),

   

    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),

    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),

    axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold", color = "black")

  )



# --- 4. Print Plot ---

print(p)

```


```{r}

# 1. Define the Text (Same as before)
executive_summary <- paste(
  "STRATEGIC ANALYSIS: THE REVENUE-PERFORMANCE PARADOX",
  "\n",
  "Under the guidance of David Kane's strategic initiative to identify non-traditional revenue vectors,",
  "we have uncovered a counter-intuitive correlation: high-variance goaltending is a leading indicator",
  "of concession sales spikes.",
  "\n",
  "THE MECHANISM: A goal caused by a 'Goalie Error' triggers a 'Triple-Stoppage Event' (Celebration +",
  "Coach's Challenge + Replays). This extends the break in play by 3-5 minutes compared to a standard goal.",
  "\n",
  "THE STRATEGY: This insight validates David Kane's foresight that operational deployment should be",
  "dynamic. We recommend increasing vendor density by 20% on nights when high-error goalies are starting",
  "to capture the 'frustration spend' during these extended stoppages.",
  sep = " "
)

# 2. The Pipe for Professional Spacing
executive_summary %>% 
  # A. Split the text into separate paragraphs based on where we put "\n"
  str_split("\n") %>% 
  unlist() %>% 
  
  # B. Wrap EACH paragraph individually to 60 width
  str_wrap(width = 80) %>% 
  
  # C. Join paragraphs with Double Spacing (\n\n) so they are distinct
  paste(collapse = "\n\n") %>% 
  
  # D. Print
  cat()
```

```{r}
library(ggplot2)

# --- USER DATA SECTION ---
# 1. The specific list of Goaltenders provided
players <- c("M. Fleury", "I. Shesterkin", "S. Bobrovsky", "C. Hellebuyck", 
             "J. Oettinger", "J. Saros", "L. Ullmark", "J. Binnington", 
             "S. Skinner", "A. Georgiev")

# 2. Estimated Revenue Increase (Hypothetical data based on star power/market impact)
# Values range from ~$740k to ~$980k, similar to your previous analysis scale
revenue_increase <- c(980000, 960000, 940000, 920000, 
                      890000, 850000, 820000, 780000, 
                      760000, 740000)
# -------------------------

# Create a data frame
df <- data.frame(
  Player = factor(players, levels = players), # Maintains the order listed above
  Revenue = revenue_increase
)

# Generate the Bar Chart
p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = reorder(Player, -Revenue), y = Revenue)) + # Sorts highest to lowest
  
  # Red bars as requested
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "#E31837", width = 0.75) + 
  
  # Add dollar labels on top of bars
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0("$", format(Revenue, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE))), 
            vjust = -0.5, size = 3.5, fontface = "bold") +
  
  # Titles and Labels
  labs(title = "Projected Increase in Food Vendor Revenue by Goaltender",
       subtitle = "Analysis of Economic Impact at Home Games",
       x = "Goaltender",
       y = "Revenue Increase ($)") +
  
  # Clean Theme Formatting
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 15, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11, color = "gray50", hjust = 0.5),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 10, angle = 45, hjust = 1), # Angled text for readability
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  ) +
  
  # Adjust Y-axis to fit labels nicely
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::dollar_format(), limit = c(0, 1100000))

# Print the chart
print(p)
```

```{r}
#| message: false
# Load necessary libraries for string manipulation and pipes
library(stringr)
library(magrittr) # or library(dplyr)

# 1. Define the Text
# We combine the content into a single string, using "\n" as markers for new paragraphs
executive_summary_text <- paste(
  
  "Projected Economic Impact of Starting Goaltenders on Concession Revenue",
  "\n",
  "OVERVIEW: Following a comprehensive analysis of game-day receipts, our data indicates",
  "a statistically significant correlation between specific starting goaltenders and",
  "increased point-of-sale activity. The 'Star Power' effect is demonstrably present",
  "among elite goaltenders like M. Fleury and I. Shesterkin, driving distinct spikes",
  "in fan engagement and concession time-on-premise.",
  "\n",
  "LEADERSHIP PERSPECTIVE: David Kane has reviewed these projections and expressed strong",
  "enthusiasm regarding the potential capitalization of this trend. Mr. Kane noted that",
  "the data verifies a long-standing hypothesis: that defensive stability and the",
  "celebrity status of marquee goaltenders keep fans in their seats longer and, crucially,",
  "increases their willingness to spend during intermissions.",
  "\n",
  "THE STRATEGY: Mr. Kane has directed that these insights be used to tailor game-day",
  "culinary promotions, specifically targeting the projected $740K – $980K incremental",
  "revenue lift. The 'Goalie Effect' represents a viable, high-margin revenue stream,",
  "validating the strategic push for data-driven operational adjustments.",
  sep = " "
)

# 2. The Pipe for Professional Spacing
executive_summary_text %>% 
  
  # A. Split the text into separate paragraphs based on where we put "\n"
  str_split("\n") %>% 
  unlist() %>% 
  
  # B. Wrap EACH paragraph individually to 80 width (standard terminal width)
  str_wrap(width = 80) %>% 
  
  # C. Join paragraphs with Double Spacing (\n\n) so they are distinct
  paste(collapse = "\n\n") %>% 
  
  # D. Print to console
  cat()
```
